title: Graceful degrade recovery and audit handoff
summary: Customer and Redwood run through a post-incident handoff: reconcile audit/evidence for compliance, agree on a graceful-degrade and rollback playbook, scope a short pilot for dedicated fallback lanes, and schedule follow-ups for benchmarks and security review.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Orion SRE), Leah Gomez (Orion Head of Platform), Ahmed Khan (Orion Security), Sofia Martinez (Product), Mike Chen (Ops)

Summary: postmortem handoff and operational runbook creation, plus audit evidence packaging for upcoming compliance review.

[00:00] Morgan Lee: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh we'll run through the RCA packet, the graceful degrade plan, and the audit handoff. hi daniel, leah, ahmed.
[00:16] Daniel Park: thanks Morgan, appreciate it. we had a lot of internal follow-up after the outage, want to make sure the artifacts are in a form our auditors can consume.
[00:24] Leah Gomez: yeah and we need clear ops steps — when to flip to fallback, how to validate responses, and what evidence to retain.
[00:35] Priya Nair: got it. i worked with eng to extract the request traces and the KV cache metrics. note: some of the keys were obfuscated in the existing dump so we redacted customer ids, but timestamps and token counts are present.
[00:49] Ahmed Khan: for compliance we need the KMS usage logs, and evidence that keys were never exported. also we need SSO login traces around the time window. can you include those?
[00:58] Morgan Lee: yes we will include KMS access logs and the SSO assertion logs — that's part of the RCA packet. i'll link the S3 archive.
[01:10] Sofia Martinez: quick context — for product we're most worried about user-facing latency and incorrect fallbacks. last time some calls degraded to an older smaller model and returned truncated completions, which our UI treated as success. we need a better detection and circuit-breaker.
[01:30] Priya Nair: right. our logs show the swap to the smaller variant triggered because the primary pool exceeded queue depth; the fallback policy executed but the validation gate didn't catch truncated outputs. i have sample traces.
[01:45] Mike Chen: and from ops we saw the autoscaler spike taking 90 seconds to provision additional capacity which is outside our SLA for spike handling.
[01:56] Priya Nair: note — that 90 seconds was exacerbated by the burst policy not firing due to a misconfigured tag on the instance group. human error on config.
[02:08] Daniel Park: ok that's helpful. so main causes: autoscale tag misconfig, fallback validation gap, and delayed KMS log retrieval?
[02:20] Morgan Lee: yes, plus a rare KV cache eviction pattern that made some responses malformed. i want to be explicit: that KV cache behavior was a race in our runtime that we patched the week after, but we should provide the exact commit and rollout window.
[02:36] Leah Gomez: please include the commit hashes and the canary rollout timing. audit wants to know when the fix was live versus the incident.
[02:46] Priya Nair: sure will add hash redacted for PII but full internal commit id in the packet.
[02:53] Ahmed Khan: on the audit evidence format — our compliance team needs machine-parsable logs, not just screenshots. CSV or JSONL preferred.
[03:04] Morgan Lee: we'll export JSONL for the traces and the KV deltas. also include a mapping doc to translate our internal event names to audit-friendly labels.
[03:16] Daniel Park: thanks. wanted to walk the graceful degrade runbook idea — we proposed two-tier fallbacks: first a validation gate that runs micro-evals on the response (length checks, safety heuristics, token distribution), then if it fails route to a dedicated fallback pool with pinned small model and truncated output handling.
[03:36] Priya Nair: yes that two-tier approach is what we sketched. important detail: the validation gate needs to be synchronous to avoid extra latency; we can keep it cheap — 1-2 token checks and a few heuristics. if validation fails, send to fallback with an explicit response flag so UI can show "degraded" state.
[03:57] Sofia Martinez: in product terms we'd rather show 'degraded' than silently accept wrong answers. ops can show a banner.
[04:05] Mike Chen: what's the latency delta on the synchronous validation?
[04:10] Priya Nair: around 12-20ms median on our infra, worst-case 45ms under heavy load — it's acceptable versus returning wrong content.
[04:19] Daniel Park: ok. and the dedicated fallback pool — is that hosted or do we need dedicated nodes? cost is a big ask for procurement.
[04:29] Morgan Lee: two options: 1) a light-weight reserved dedicated pool for critical traffic (Reserved/Dedicated model) — predictable but costed; 2) a policy-based hosted fallback using cheaper quantized variants we already host. for strict isolation and guaranteed throughput, dedicated is best. for budget, hosted fallback works.
[04:48] Leah Gomez: procurement leans to hosted first but security wants dedicated because of data residency and audit controls.
[04:55] Ahmed Khan: yes we need to validate the hosted path with policy controls — data retention windows, KMS integration, and whether logs are exported to their tenant S3.
[05:06] Morgan Lee: hosted supports tenant-isolated logs and KMS integration via our customer KMS envelope. we do provide HSM-backed key handling for Private deployments but hosted uses our KMS with per-tenant encryptions keys. we can add extra retention TTL options.
[05:22] Ahmed Khan: can you confirm keys are never accessible to Redwood ops? we need 'no-key-access' proof.
[05:29] Priya Nair: for Private and Dedicated - customers manage KMS; for hosted the KMS is managed but key material isn't exported. we will include the KMS audit showing admin access patterns during the incident window.
[05:41] Daniel Park: good. let's talk about the rollback/playbook: we want a clearly defined 'safe stop' — e.g., pause routing to primary, flip to fallback pool, and run smoke tests for five minutes, then scale or re-run canary. can you outline that sequence?
[05:55] Priya Nair: sequence draft: 1) detect and confirm spike via latency + error thresholds, 2) run automated smoke validation, 3) if majority failing, mark primary unhealthy, 4) route a small canary (5%) to fallback pool, 5) if canary passes, ramp to 50% then full. each step has TTL and rollback windows.
[06:16] Sofia Martinez: who executes step 3 — our ops or Redwood? we need playbook ownership so auditors can see sign-offs.
[06:25] Morgan Lee: we recommend initial execution by Orion ops with Redwood in assist mode; pilot will shift to automated policies later. we'll include a sign-off table and contact list in the runbook.
[06:36] Mike Chen: about validation gates — are these run inside the runtime or as a separate sidecar service?
[06:42] Priya Nair: lightweight validators are a sidecar function fronting the runtime; this lets you update heuristics without touching the model infra. we already ship a validator module that you can configure (JSON rules).
[06:56] Daniel Park: ok small question about evidence retention: auditors will request last 90 days of model config, key rotations, and rollout events. can you provide an export?
[07:07] Morgan Lee: yes we can provide config history and rotation events; we keep 365 days by default for enterprise customers, and will bundle the 90-day subset.
[07:16] Ahmed Khan: excellent. also please note time zones in timestamps — auditors will ask for local timestamps and UTC, so include both.
[07:25] Priya Nair: we'll provide both in the JSONL.
[07:29] [07:29] Priya Nair: (laughs) sorry accidental duplicate timestamp there.
[07:33] Leah Gomez: small nit — the UI treating truncated as success was a product bug; we'll push a UX change to detect truncation flag in the response and present fallback messaging. that reduces risk of silent bad content.
[07:46] Sofia Martinez: yes product will implement that by next sprint. we'll coordinate with Redwood so the API includes explicit response flags on fallback.
[07:54] Morgan Lee: agreed. we'll expose a 'redwood.degrade.reason' field in the response for the pilot.
[08:00] Daniel Park: let's scope the pilot: 2 weeks, start week of 2027-08-18, traffic gradually ramped to 10% fallback routing during peak hours, smoke tests daily, and a security review mid-pilot.
[08:13] Morgan Lee: sounds good. we should also run a simulated KV cache eviction test in staging to validate the patched runtime under load.
[08:22] Priya Nair: we can run the eviction sim and share the load profile. one caveat: the eviction bug manifested only with mixed-sequence workloads; we need test prompts that mimic production. please share a sanitized prompt corpus.
[08:36] Mike Chen: we can extract sanitized prompts and remove PII; we'll deliver that to Priya by EOD tomorrow.
[08:44] Daniel Park: about cost estimation for dedicated fallback — can you give a rough monthly number for 2 reserved rtx-class nodes?
[08:52] Morgan Lee: rough back-of-envelope: $9k–12k per month for two reserved nodes depending on region and commitment. exact quote will be in the commercial packet.
[09:02] Leah Gomez: procurement will need that spelled out — include the elasticity options and auto-suspend for off-hours.
[09:10] Priya Nair: action: i'll include a bill of materials for both hosted fallback and dedicated reserved capacity with expected QPS and token cost estimates.
[09:20] Ahmed Khan: major security question: during the incident did any logs leave our tenant boundaries? we've got to be certain.
[09:28] Morgan Lee: no logs exported outside of our tenant S3 bucket; we audited transfer events and none were pushed to external buckets. we'll include the audit trail.
[09:37] Daniel Park: i also want an explicit timeline entry: when the patch was built, when it was canaried, and when full rollout happened. auditors like to see who approved each step.
[09:47] Priya Nair: patch built 2027-06-21 03:14 UTC, canary started 2027-06-22 09:00 UTC (20% for 2 hours), full rollout 2027-06-22 11:30 UTC. approvals by eng lead (name in packet).
[10:01] Sofia Martinez: that looks good. any other outstanding technical unknowns?
[10:08] Daniel Park: one more — what's the expected impact on latency when we route to the fallback pool? our SLA is 200ms p95.
[10:15] Priya Nair: fallback pool with a smaller quantized model typically adds 40–80ms median, p95 under 200ms for short contexts; we'll include p50/p95 numbers from the smoke runs.
[10:28] Morgan Lee: okay let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:32] Morgan Lee: Redwood: compile RCA packet with JSONL traces, KMS audit, commit hashes. redwood owner: Morgan. due 2027-08-06.
[10:40] Morgan Lee: Redwood SE (Priya): graceful-degrade runbook draft, validation rule set, and simulated KV eviction test results. due 2027-08-11.
[10:49] Daniel Park: Orion: provide sanitized prompt corpus and confirm routing policy for pilot, owner Mike and Daniel, due 2027-08-05 for corpus, 2027-08-12 for routing confirmation.
[10:59] Ahmed Khan: Orion Security: provide audit evidence checklist and required formats. due 2027-08-09.
[11:06] Morgan Lee: we'll schedule security deep dive for 2027-08-10, i'll send a calendar invite after this call.
[11:12] Leah Gomez: please include legal/procurement in the invite so we can fast-track contract for dedicated if needed.
[11:18] Morgan Lee: noted. final question — are there any blockers to Redwood sharing the RCA packet?
[11:23] Ahmed Khan: only that we need the logs redacted for PII and include migration proofs; otherwise good.
[11:31] Priya Nair: we'll redact PII and provide a mapping file for the redactions.
[11:36] Morgan Lee: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and the invite.
[11:41] Daniel Park: thanks all. appreciate the thorough follow-up.
[11:45] Sofia Martinez: thanks, bye.
[11:47] End of transcript.

Notes:
- There's occasional mis-hearings in the auto-transcript (e.g., 'KV' sometimes shows up as 'k v', and 'canary' was transcribed as 'canarie' in one chunk). Manual QA will correct important artifacts in the RCA packet.
- References to specific commit hashes and internal names are redacted in this transcript for security; full values in the secured packet.
